text:
Eeli Tolvanen still has a heavy shot (89 mph top speed, 88th percentile), and in his first season in New York he has 4 goals and 6 points in 20 games. He snapped a slump on Nov 3 against St. Louis with a goal and an assist, the goal into an empty net.

The role is small and getting smaller: about 12 minutes a night on the season, 11:18 over his last ten, with a 6:30 night in Edmonton. His shooting (17.4%) is above his usual, and his own chances over the last ten have been thin, so expect the goal pace to settle. The Rangers have scored 4.29 more goals than expected with him on the ice, which flatters him. Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level in Seattle last season, playing with weak teammates and not creating much. The upside is the release that brought him 7 goals at the 2025 World Championship for Finland. Getting him more of the puck is how New York gets it.
headline: Eeli Tolvanen's shot, in a smaller role
